races.title: State Assembly, District 40
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Pilar Schiavo
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented California's 40th Assembly District since December 2022. Before that she was a small business owner and a Nurse Advocate with the California Nurses Association, and co-founded a nonprofit serving people experiencing homelessness. She defeated Republican incumbent Suzette Martinez Valladares in 2022.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter and YIMBY Action.
Her campaign website says she is supported by nurses, teachers, firefighters, police officers, deputy sheriffs and healthcare workers. This is the campaign's own claim.
Wikipedia says the Los Angeles Times endorsed her in 2022.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Schiavo grew up or when she moved to California as an adult. We found no documented public statements by her on data centers or on limiting development. We found no verified bill sponsorships or official actions tied to specific issues such as homestead taxes, guns, immigration, abortion, school choice or policing. Her campaign site claims she voted against tax increases and authored bills cutting building fees, but the pages we had did not let us confirm either claim. Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation list was empty in the page we read. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or foreign-government-funded travel.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2022, with a seat on the Budget Committee. Earlier she worked about twenty years in the labor movement as an organizer and Nurse Advocate with the California Nurses Association, and she was a small business owner.
qual.why: She has held legislative office for about three years, and her career before that was in labor organizing and health-policy advocacy. Committee seats and her chair of the Military and Veterans Affairs Committee were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Rickey Tracy Hayes II
cands.bio: Marine Corps veteran, former custody officer and police officer, and electrical engineer working in energy infrastructure. Lives in Santa Clarita. Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 40 in 2026. He has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Hayes lists endorsements from Reform California, State Senator Suzette Valladares, LA County Supervisor Kathryn Barger, LA City Councilman John Lee, IBEW Local 18, Santa Clarita City Councilman Jason Gibbs, former Assemblyman and Santa Clarita Mayor Cameron Smyth, Porter Ranch Neighborhood Councilwoman Becky Leveque, and Mike DeLorenzo of Santa Clarita Studios. Ballotpedia also lists Reform California among his endorsers, along with several voter-guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Hayes holding public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found nothing on his positions on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor purchases of land and homes, H-1B visas and immigration enforcement, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His survey says he wants to restore local control of zoning and build more housing, but gives no specifics. We could not confirm his birth year, his exact birthplace (Compton or Long Beach), his employers or dates of service in the Marine Corps, police work or energy industry, or any news coverage of him beyond his own survey answers.

local.label: Roots 100: In his Ballotpedia survey Hayes says he was born and raised with deep roots in Compton and Long Beach, and has lived in Santa Clarita for more than 13 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps, then worked as a custody officer and police officer, and later as an electrical engineer and energy infrastructure professional. No elected or legislative office is documented.
qual.why: There is no legislative, budget or policy work on record. His law enforcement and engineering careers are real work but not closely tied to writing law and budgets, so he scores in the low range.

back-police-order.evidence: In his Ballotpedia survey he said he wants to restore public safety by enforcing California laws, rolling back Prop 47, upholding Prop 36, and making theft and hard drug use crimes. He also said enforcement would help move homeless people into treatment.
